n.story:
In your role, AI acts as a silent, highly efficient partner that manages the 'breath' of the kiln. While the physical nature of handling timber remains a human task, the science of the drying process has become significantly more automated. You no longer need to manually adjust temperatures or guess the moisture content of a stack; IoT sensors and AI-driven kiln schedules now optimize ventilation and heat in real-time to prevent warping and defects. This precision not only saves energy but ensures a higher quality yield from every batch.

Your workday has shifted from constant monitoring of dials to high-level oversight. You use AI-powered expert systems to identify wood species and predict how specific timber products will behave under different construction conditions. When the system flags a potential drying defect, you use your tactile expertise to verify the internal structural integrity. You have evolved from a machine operator into a technical specialist who blends traditional woodcraft knowledge with advanced thermodynamic data.

Optimization of drying cycles for rare or high-value wood

AI sensors will now instantly identify wood species and moisture content, automatically calculating the exact chemical mix and pressure required for a perfect treat.
